title: Twenty Terms and One Early Bell
subtitle: 习惯与自律 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 习惯与自律（生活与学习·良好习惯与自律）
meta: 主题语境：习惯与自律（生活与学习·良好习惯与自律）　|　核心词汇：discipline　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 discipline 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1945 the headmaster ① kept a discipline that no parent in the town would have understood, and he said the keeping was the whole of the school. The ② discipline, meaning the self-control and not the subject, ran twenty terms and stayed unpraised in the report; a discipline, he said, is the only thing in a school that is judged by how long it is left unmentioned.

Every ③ discipline in that school had the same early bell at the start of it, and the ④ discipline at the end, meaning the one they kept for the oldest forms and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A discipline, his deputy said, is nine parts habit and one part somebody willing to keep; the headmaster said the habit is the part that fills twenty terms.

The registrar meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ the discipline was the whole of the syllabus, meaning the subject and not the self-control. The ⑥ discipline, meaning the subject and not any of that, is the only thing in a syllabus that everybody timetables and nobody defines; discipline, she said, is either something you keep or the only word that means both a self-control and a subject. She said the subject is the part they remember.

By 1954 the ⑦ discipline had become a line in a handbook, and the handbook had become an argument about the early bell. The ⑧ discipline of the whole thing, the headmaster wrote in May, was one school and twenty terms of keeping; discipline, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to keep. She said the keeping was never mentioned.

The ⑨ discipline I remember is the one at the end, which was praised in 1968 and is still described as the quietest in the school. A ⑩ discipline, the deputy said in 1970, is the only thing that improves by being kept; every discipline, she said, is a subject that has agreed to look like a self-control. She said the subject was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 纪律；自律（指学校里守住的那一份）
B. n. 自律（指那份自我约束本身，与那门学科相对）
C. 固定搭配：keep a discipline 保持一份自律
D. n. 纪律（指留给高年级用的那一份）
E. n. 纪律；自律（抽象总称，指一所学校的全部训练）
F. n. 学科；科目（指课程表上排定的那一门）
G. n. 训练；管教（指手册里写到、被规定的那套）
H. n. 学科（抽象总称，指人人排课却无人定义的那一门）

items.q: kept a discipline that no parent in the town would have understood
The discipline, meaning the self-control and not the subject
the discipline was the whole of the syllabus
the discipline had become a line in a handbook
The discipline of the whole thing
A discipline, the deputy said in 1970

answers.why: keep a discipline 意为“保持一份自律”，1945 年校长守着一份全镇没有一位家长能理解的自律。
discipline 意为“自律”，指那份自我约束本身而不是那门学科，它守了二十个学期而在报告里无人称道。
discipline 意为“纪律、自律”，指那所学校里每一份自律，每一份开端都是同一声清早的铃。
discipline 意为“纪律”，指留给高年级用的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
discipline 意为“学科、科目”，指课程表上排定的那一门，注册主任说这门学科就是那份课程大纲的全部。
discipline 意为“学科”，指人人排课却无人定义的那一门而不是那份自我约束，是大纲里人人都排课、却无人定义的那一门。
discipline 意为“训练、管教”，指手册里写到、被规定的那套，到 1954 年这套训练成了手册里的一行。
discipline 意为“纪律、自律”，校长五月写道，整件事的训练是一所学校和二十个学期的坚持。
discipline 意为“自律”，我记得的是末尾那一份，1968 年受到称道，至今仍被说成学校里最安静的一份。
discipline 为抽象总称，副校长 1970 年说，一份自律是唯一会因为被坚持下去而变得更好的东西。
